title: Gallery
text: Nomograms come in many shapes. This page starts by building one by hand, from nothing but curves, and then shows a range of others — each with the code that draws it.

title: A chart built piece by piece
text: Every chart in this package is a set of Scales: curves that take a value to a point on the page. The constructions — additive_nomogram and the rest — only work out those curves for you. You can write them yourself, and the result solves, checks and draws like any other chart. Here is a classic …

title: Logarithmic scales
text:
The commonest nomogram: a product, drawn on three parallel logarithmic scales by multiplicative_nomogram. Ohm's law over five decades of current: using Nomograms

title: Building charts
text: A nomogram asserts one thing: that a point taken from each scale lies on a single straight line. So every chart in this package is a set of parametric curves value -> (x, y) (Scale), and each construction below is a way of choosing curves that makes that collinearity agree with a relation. title: Anything else, from the determinant
text: The two named constructions are particular solutions of the collinearity condition. determinant_nomogram takes any other one you can write down: give each variable a curve, and the combined bounding box is measured and mapped onto the canvas for you. title: Reshaping, for free
text: An affine map preserves collinearity, which is why fitting curves to the canvas is safe. Projective maps preserve it too, and they are a much larger family — they can turn parallel scales into converging ones and redistribute spacing along an axis. title: Nomograms.Nomograms
text: Nomograms Build, solve and render nomograms (alignment charts). A nomogram is an analog computer printed on paper. title: Nomograms.DEFAULT_ISOPLETH_COLORS
text: DEFAULT_ISOPLETH_COLORS Blue, orange, aqua. Three, not more, and in this order: every isopleth on a chart is visible at once, so all three pairs have to stay apart under colour-vision deficiency, and no fourth hue holds up once all pairs are in play. title: Nomograms.DEFAULT_ISOPLETH_DASHES

title: Bibliography
text: Nomography is a nineteenth-century subject with a long textbook tradition. These are the works this documentation leans on, and where to go for more.

title: The founding text
text: Maurice d'Ocagne. Traité de nomographie. Théorie des abaques, applications pratiques. Paris: Gauthier-Villars, 1899. text: L. Ivan Epstein. Nomography. New York: Interscience, 1958.Edward Otto. Nomography. New York: Macmillan, 1963. title: Nomograms.jl
text: A nomogram is an analog computer printed on paper. Lay a straightedge through the values you know, and it crosses the remaining scale at the answer — no power, no keystrokes, just geometry. Nomograms.jl builds them from the formulas you already use, solves them numerically, and draws them as SVG …

title: Four or more variables
text: One alignment line can relate only three scales. Past that there are two ways on: chain charts together through a shared scale, or let one point carry two variables at once. auto_nomogram builds chains by itself for formulas that allow them; this page is about building either by hand.
